passage:
"Joseph, you've barely touched your food," said Reena, setting her tray down.
"Everyone's talking about the fest." He stirred his rice. "Nobody's asked about Ajji. She died three weeks ago."
"I didn't know if I should bring it up."
"It's like the whole class pressed play and I'm still on pause. I thought nobody cared."
"I do care. I just didn't want to hurt you by asking."
Joseph looked up. "It hurts more when nobody asks. Could you ask how I'm doing, sometimes? And sit with me at lunch this week?"
"Yes. Both. And I'll tell Meena and Sam, if you want."
"Please," he said, and it was the first breath that had gone all the way down in days.

qa.q: How long ago had Joseph's grandmother died?
What did Joseph feel while the class talked about the fest?
qa.a: Frozen and unseen, as if everyone else had pressed play while he stayed on pause.

qa.q: What did Joseph do that helped, and how?
qa.a: He told Reena plainly what he needed, being asked how he was and having company at lunch.

qa.q: Why might Reena not have asked about Joseph's grandmother earlier?
qa.a: She feared that asking would hurt him, so her silence came from caution rather than not caring.

grounding: Classmates return to normal life while the protagonist feels frozen; naming what he needs to a peer opens support.

passage:
Class mentor's note, second-year B.Com.

Shankar came back three weeks after his mother's death. The class had moved on: fest posters, internship forms, jokes in the back row. Nobody asked him anything. In my tutorial he sat by the window and did not open his notebook. When a classmate laughed loudly, he flinched.

I asked him to stay after class. He said, "It's like I'm invisible. Everyone's normal and I'm frozen." Then, "Maybe they don't care."

I said they probably care but don't know what to say, and that grief is invisible to most people unless someone names it. I asked if there were one or two classmates he trusted.

He named Gautam and Deepak. The next day he told them. Gautam now saves him a seat and asks, most mornings, "How's today?" Shankar says it helps.

- Pallavi

qa.q: Who did Shankar name as classmates he trusted?
What was Shankar feeling when he said "It's like I'm invisible"?
qa.a: Shankar felt hurt and frozen in grief, and lonely because nobody asked him anything.

qa.q: How did Pallavi help Shankar change the situation?
qa.a: Pallavi explained that people often don't know what to say and helped him pick one or two classmates to tell, so they could support him.

qa.q: How might Gautam have seen Shankar before being told?
qa.a: Gautam may simply not have known what to say, and so said nothing, even though Gautam cared.

grounding: The mentor's note shows a grieving young man hurt that classmates don't ask, and helped to tell one or two people what he needs.

passage:
Monday night

It's been a month since Appa died and today the whole class was talking about the fest. Somebody asked me what theme our group should pick, like nothing happened. Nobody has said his name since I came back. I'm Rukmini, and I've started eating lunch in the library so I don't have to smile.

I thought maybe nobody cares. Then Shreya caught up with me at the bus stop. She said, "I wanted to ask about your appa but I didn't know if it would upset you."

I nearly cried with relief. I told her the truth: "I want people to ask. Even if I cry. Not asking is worse." She said she'd tell a couple of the others, if I wanted. I said yes.

Tomorrow I'll eat lunch in the canteen again. Shreya's saving a seat.

qa.q: Where has Rukmini been eating lunch?
qa.a: Rukmini has been eating lunch in the library.

qa.q: What did Rukmini feel when Shreya spoke at the bus stop?
qa.a: Rukmini felt a wave of relief, nearly crying, because someone finally showed they cared.

qa.q: What did Rukmini say that helped others know how to support her?
qa.a: Rukmini told Shreya plainly that people should ask, even if it brings tears, and agreed that Shreya could tell a couple of others.

qa.q: How had Shreya seen the situation before speaking?
qa.a: Shreya cared but was afraid that asking about Appa would upset Rukmini, so she stayed quiet.

grounding: The diary shows a grieving young person hurt that classmates don't ask, who learns that telling one person what they need changes things.
